explanation: Defense mechanisms like denial act as psychological buffers, shielding the individual from sudden, unbearable emotional shocks. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which medical term is used for a freely movable joint?

options.A: Synarthrosis
options.B: Syndesmosis
options.C: Amphiarthrosis
options.D: Diarthrosis

explanation: Well done! A 'diarthrosis' is a freely movable joint (think of your dancing hips or swinging arms). It matches up with our synovial joints.

question: What is a major benefit of having a standard list of medications in a clinic?

options.A: It guarantees that pharmaceutical companies make higher profits
options.B: It forces patients to buy medications outside the hospital
options.C: It reduces dispensing errors and simplifies inventory management
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for qualified pharmacists

explanation: That's right! Using a smaller, familiar group of drugs keeps storage organized and helps prevent medication mix-ups.

question: What is a common myth about nursing work in subacute facilities?

options.A: It is merely custodial and does not require strong clinical assessment skills
options.B: It involves managing high-tech life support equipment in trauma bays
options.C: It focuses solely on discharging patients within twelve hours of arrival
options.D: It requires zero collaboration with physical or occupational therapists

explanation: Spot on. Some people wrongly think subacute care is just basic babysitting, missing the real clinical skills and monitoring required.

question: What is the main reason for placing a Word catheter after draining a Bartholin cyst?

options.A: To freeze and destroy the remaining cyst wall cells
options.B: To pump liquid antibiotics directly inside the cavity
options.C: To keep the new drainage opening open so a fresh duct can form
options.D: To permanently stop all fluid production in the body

explanation: The Word catheter has a tiny balloon at the tip and stays in for a few weeks. It keeps the wound open so it can heal into a permanent, normal drainage pathway.

question: What is a major challenge for injection safety in resource-limited settings like Nigeria?

options.A: An excessive surplus of modern safety-engineered syringes
options.B: Supply chain disruptions and shortages of safety devices
options.C: Complete lack of any national health guidelines or policies
options.D: Patients refusing to accept any injections from trained nurses

explanation: When clinics face stockouts of safety gear and syringes, it makes ideal infection control a tough daily battle for nurses.

question: Which lab test is primarily used to monitor a patient who is taking heparin?

options.A: Prothrombin Time (PT)
options.B: Serum electrolyte panel
options.C: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT)
options.D: Total red blood cell count

explanation: We use the aPTT test to keep a close eye on heparin therapy and make sure our patient's blood is clotting at a safe, therapeutic level.

question: Why do some families in impoverished areas marry off their young daughters early?

options.A: To reduce family financial burdens and secure alliances
options.B: To prevent the girl from learning professional trades
options.C: To comply with mandatory international health policies
options.D: To guarantee the girl completes her university degree

explanation: That's correct. Extreme poverty and old traditions sometimes lead families to view young girls as economic solutions through early marriage.

question: Which descriptive statistic represents the exact middle value of a dataset?

options.A: Mode
options.B: Median
options.C: Mean
options.D: Standard deviation

explanation: The median splits the dataset directly in half, with fifty percent of the values above it and fifty percent below. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why does a nurse use the back of the hand when checking skin temperature over a swollen joint?

options.A: It is required by standard infection control guidelines for wound care
options.B: The skin on the dorsal hand is thinner and more sensitive to temperature changes
options.C: It prevents the patient from feeling intimidated by a direct palm touch
options.D: The palm is too warm to detect minor differences in body heat

explanation: The thin skin on the back of the hand is much better at detecting subtle variations in local skin warmth. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why do teenage girls often have irregular periods in the first few years after starting menstruation?

options.A: The uterus is physically too small to hold a normal amount of blood.
options.B: The brain-ovary communication loop is still maturing, leading to irregular ovulation.
options.C: Increased physical activity stops the pituitary gland from working.
options.D: Dietary changes completely block the action of estrogen in the body.

explanation: It takes time for the body's hormonal feedback system to find its rhythm after menarche, which is why irregular cycles are totally normal at first.

question: Which virus is notorious for surviving on medical equipment and surfaces for days, making it very easy to spread if equipment is reused?

options.A: Influenza Virus
options.B: Streptococcus Pneumoniae
options.C: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.D: Hepatitis B Virus

explanation: Hepatitis B is a tough survivor and can live on surfaces and tools outside the body for days. That's why strict sterilization and single-use rules are non-negotiable.

question: Which screening is especially important before starting a patient on a strict low-calorie diet?

options.A: Measuring adult visual acuity levels
options.B: Testing for chronic seasonal allergies
options.C: Evaluating natural hair color changes
options.D: Screening for history of eating disorders

explanation: Correct! Strict calorie tracking can trigger unhealthy eating habits, so checking a patient's history first is an important safety step.

question: What does the letter 'C' stand for in the ABCDE primary survey framework?

options.A: Comfort
options.B: Coughing
options.C: Circulation
options.D: Confusion

explanation: In the ABCDE emergency assessment, C stands for circulation, which involves checking pulses, bleeding, and perfusion. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h2)

question: What minimum level of medication adherence is needed to keep HIV fully suppressed over the long term?

options.A: Around 50%
options.B: Exactly 20%
options.C: At least 95%
options.D: Only on weekends

explanation: You got it! HIV treatment requires consistency. Taking at least 95% of doses on schedule keeps the virus cornered and unable to fight back.

question: In nursing, what does 'bundling care' mean when it comes to helping patients sleep?

options.A: Administering all daily medications at the exact same morning hour
options.B: Wrapping the patient tightly in heavy wool blankets
options.C: Grouping multiple care tasks together to reduce the number of times a patient is woken up
options.D: Sharing night shift duties evenly between nurses and assistants

explanation: Instead of waking your patient up every hour for a different task, you combine vital signs, meds, and dressings into one visit. That way, they get longer stretches of uninterrupted sleep!

question: Which bed position is best for instantly helping an out-of-breath patient expand their lungs?

options.A: Trendelenburg position
options.B: High-Fowler's position
options.C: Prone lying position
options.D: Flat supine position

explanation: Sitting upright in High-Fowler's position uses gravity to push abdominal organs downward, giving the lungs more room to fill with air. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why is it important for nurses to know the physical signs of grief?

options.A: To prevent mistaking normal grief reactions for physical illness
options.B: To stop patients from feeling any physical pain
options.C: To prove that grief is purely a physical disease
options.D: To prescribe strong antibiotics for chest tightness

explanation: Spot on! Recognizing that things like stomach ache or trouble sleeping are normal grief signs stops unnecessary medical tests and reassures the patient.

question: What major staffing headache in Nigerian healthcare do polyvalent nurses help solve?

options.A: A lack of patients seeking medical treatment
options.B: Shortages of specialized nursing personnel in facilities
options.C: An oversupply of doctors in rural health centers
options.D: Excessive funding for primary health care clinics

explanation: You got it! They are a wonderful solution for bridging the gap where specialized nurses are hard to find.
